answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each agent to stake a deposit tied to a verifiable work history before it can trade. Like a meadow that only feeds grazers who return each season, reputation accrues slowly through attested transactions, so a fresh fake identity starts with zero trust. New entrants pass through a narrow inlet: a small probationary quota with rate limits, and only after consistent honest behavior do they climb to a terrace of full trading rights. Creating thousands of identities then costs deposits and time, while honest agents keep their earned standing.
